summary: Flame in Freefall serves as a dashboard for combustion scenarios in microgravity. For each situation, it outlines what NASA’s combustion data reveals, the level of confidence that can be placed in this information, and which experiments are still needed.
details:
Flame in Freefall is a project built as a stack of layers, each one feeding the next, to answer the challenge of the same name.

  • No invented number: this is rule number 1, the one the whole project is built around. Every value shown traces back to a source file and a row or page, and each file is itself linked to its original source. Values read from a figure are flagged.
  • A traceable confidence engine: all source files are fed into a Python engine built on two axes (evidence, agreement), combined in a matrix and then capped by explicit rules. The result is a confidence level, ranked into one of four categories (very low, low, medium, high).
  • The AI is boxed in: Gemini only routes a question to a scenario and rewrites facts the engine has already produced. Any text containing a number that is not in the engine’s facts is rejected, and the rule-based text is shown instead.
  • A web dashboard, built with Next.js, serves as the interface for the whole system.
